requirement: A `{req}` opening fence MAY contain four or more colons. Habeas MUST accept opening fences of any length of at least three colons. A colon-only line with fewer colons than the opener MUST remain inside the requirement body, allowing a nested colon directive. A closing fence outside a fenced code example with at least as many colons as the opener MUST end the body.
rationale:
I found no gaps. Each obligation has code carrying an {impl} reference and a test that asserts its outcome.

**Obligations and code**
- **Accept opening fences of any length of at least three colons.** `colon_fence` in `src/lib.rs` returns a length only when there are at least 3 leading colons and no more than 3 spaces of indentation. `definition_blocks` in `src/lib.rs` uses it for `{req}`, `{example}` and `{definition}` fences. `opening_fence` in `src/fenced.rs` does the same for reference fences. All of these carry {impl} references to the requirement.
- **Keep shorter colon-only lines inside the body.** The closer search in `definition_blocks` only accepts a line whose colon count is at least the opener's and whose remainder is blank. `closes` and `find_fences` in `src/fenced.rs` apply the same rule. A shorter `:::` line is therefore not a closer, so a nested `:::{note}` stays in the body.
- **Close on a line with at least as many colons, outside a fenced code example.** `definition_blocks` and `find_fences` skip candidate lines that are in protected code ranges, using `overlaps_protected` and `.protected` respectively. The first remaining line with `count >= fence_length` ends the body.

**Tests**
- `validates_four_or_more_colon_fences_and_longer_closers` in `src/evidence.rs` covers openers of 4 and 7 colons. It covers closers of equal and longer length, and a nested `:::{note}` that stays in the body.
- `a_longer_colon_fence_contains_a_shorter_nested_directive` in `src/lib.rs` asserts the exact body span for a 4-colon opener with a nested 3-colon directive. It also checks that the text after the closer is outside the body.
- `colon_requirement_span_includes_markdown_and_excludes_following_text` in `src/evidence.rs` puts `:::` inside a code fence in the body. The body still runs to the real closer.
- `markdown_fences_close_with_enough_colons_and_skip_code` in `src/fenced.rs` covers the reference-fence path, including a protected `:::{cite}` line inside a code fence.

The MAY clause imposes nothing to check. I saw no unspecified behavior beyond what the text describes.
